 Highlights
 CCI approved Xavier Niel's plan to acquire 16.2% of Vodafone Group Plc.
 Niel is making the acquisition through his family investment vehicle, Vega SAS.
 Vega SAS will become Vodafone's largest shareholder after the deal concludes.
 The acquisition is valued at approximately 4.4 billion pounds (5.1 billion euros).
 NEW DELHI: The Competition Commission of India ( CCI ) has cleared French billionaire Xavier Niel 's proposal to acquire a 16.2% stake in Vodafone Group Plc . Niel is acquiring the stake through his family investment vehicle, Vega SAS , a wholly-owned subsidiary of Maya SAS.
Vega SAS, which has no business presence in India, will become Vodafone's largest shareholder after the transaction closes. Vodafone Group, a European and African telecommunications company, provides fixed and mobile services in India through Vodafone Idea Ltd.
 In July, Vega SAS announced a binding agreement with Emirates Telecommunications Group Co PJSC for the acquisition, valued at approximately 4.4 billion pounds (5.1 billion euros). The fair trade regulator, CCI, confirmed its approval of the proposed deal in a release on Friday and via a post on X.
 Advt 
 Vodafone has undertaken business restructuring in recent years. This includes selling its Italian and Spanish operations and its 50% stake in its Dutch joint venture, alongside merging with Three to establish the UK's largest mobile operator.
